title: Private sector and public sector in a mixed economy
notes: Authored 2026-10-06 under standard v0.2.0-draft. All claims are provenance generated_gap, verification unverified.

blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Classify business enterprises between the private sector and the public sector in a mixed economy.

blocks.heading: Private sector and public sector
blocks.text: The private sector is the part of a mixed economy owned and controlled by individuals or companies, usually run for profit. The public sector is the part owned and controlled by the state, usually run to provide services the population needs rather than to profit. A mixed economy is one that contains both, and Namibia's economy is mixed: Oshakati Premier Juice, a private juice processor, sits in the private sector; NamWater, the state-owned water utility, sits in the public sector.

blocks.heading: The features that separate the two sectors
blocks.text:
Three features tell the sectors apart. Ownership: private-sector businesses belong to private owners or shareholders, whereas public-sector organisations belong to the state. Main aim: private-sector businesses are usually run for profit, whereas public-sector organisations usually aim to provide a service the population needs. Control: private owners and shareholders direct their own businesses, whereas government ministers and officials direct the public sector.

Applying the features settles any case. A Walvis Bay fishing company owned by a family and run for profit is private sector on all three features. A state school is public sector on all three. Outside the region the test works the same way: in the United Kingdom, the National Health Service is public sector on ownership, aim and control, while a family-run London restaurant is private sector. Ownership, aim and control decide the classification together, which is why sorting a business between the sectors gives one answer, not three.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: Topic 1.1 covered why business activity exists and how value is added; this topic sorts the businesses doing it into sectors. Topic 1.3 examines how businesses grow - a private juice processor and a state water utility grow in different ways, because their owners and aims differ.
